thread:
Maria: Heads-up — int8-v3 rollout results for rwd-lite-3b are in. quick summary below, long-doc slice shows small quality drift vs fp16 on coherence and citation density. dropping here so we can decide rollback/fallback rules.

Kai: numbers pls? :eyes:

Maria: paste of aggregated metrics (30m micro-burn)
```
slice: long-doc (>1k tokens)
traffic: 10% traffic, 30m
metrics:
  ppl(fp16): 11.2
  ppl(int8): 11.5
  top5_overlap: 0.62
  kl_divergence: 0.18
  halluc_rate (QA probe): 0.032 -> baseline 0.021 (+0.011)
  answer_empathy_score: -0.03 relative
```

Devon: ok not huge but noticeable. KL 0.18 < our usual 0.25 threshold, but halluc_rate moved by +0.011 which is ~50% relative increase. what are our auto-fallback rules? we shouldn't flip on noise.

Maria: exactly. proposal: add a drift-aware fallback that combines three signals with hysteresis
- Relative hallucation increase > 30% sustained for T_window
- OR top5_overlap < 0.6 sustained for T_window
- OR KL_divergence > 0.25
T_window proposal = 15m with smoothing (EWMA alpha=0.2)
If triggered: fractional rollback -> reduce traffic by 50% immediately and start 30m recovery check, if still bad then full fallback to fp16.

Lee: can we be more conservative for long-docs? those slices have more variance. suggestion: require 2 consecutive 15m windows (i.e., 30m sustained) for hallucation signal, but keep KL single-window.

Kai: +1 to Lee. Also add absolute minimum delta check (e.g., delta > 0.008 absolute) to avoid tiny relative spikes on low baselines.

Maria: updated rule (pseudo-yaml):
```
fallback_policy:
  signals:
    - name: kl
      op: '>'
      thresh: 0.25
      window: 15m
      require_consecutive: 1
    - name: top5_overlap
      op: '<'
      thresh: 0.6
      window: 15m
      require_consecutive: 1
    - name: halluc_rate_delta
      op: '>'
      thresh_relative: 0.30
      thresh_absolute: 0.008
      window: 15m
      require_consecutive: 2
  action_on_trigger:
    - reduce_traffic: 50%
    - evaluate_after: 30m
    - if_still_bad: fallback_to: fp16
  smoothing: ewma_alpha: 0.2
```

Devon: sounds reasonable. need to ensure metrics emitted at 1m granularity so ewma works. who owns the metric pipeline for halluc_rate? @ops-bot?

ops-bot: metric pipeline: halluc_rate probe is emitted by eval-service every 60s for configured slices. alerting bucket available at /observability/rollouts/halluc_rate.

Lee: also add a safety-net: if any slice crosses absolute halluc_rate > 0.06, immediate full fallback (no fractional) — that prevents severe regressions.

Kai: good call.

Maria: we should also capture a small sample of requests to attach to the rollout incident (4k tokens window) — saves triage time. add sample_policy: random 1% + deterministic seed for repeatability.

Devon: recommend a staged promotion path: hold at 10% for 2h micro-burn, then 30% for 4h, then 100%. each step gated by the same fallback policy and a manual sign-off for long-doc critical customers.

Maria: agreed. I can push the config to staging. deploy-bot can you run a dry-run validation of the policy yaml?

deploy-bot: validation OK. no schema errors. preview diff: - traffic: 10% -> policy live (staging)

Kai: scheduling note: update the console dashboard to show KL and top5_overlap by slice (long-doc, short-doc, chat). tagging alert runbook link.

Maria: I'll add the runbook summary and create a tiny alert: "int8-v3 long-doc drift" with severity=high if policy triggers fallback.

Lee: plan accepted. next-actions: Maria push to staging, Devon validate sampled requests, Kai update dashboard, ops confirm metric cadence. meet back in 2h.

Maria: thanks all. summary pinned to thread: hold at 10%, apply drift-aware fallback policy (as above), immediate full fallback if halluc_rate > 0.06, fractional backoff then evaluate if sustained. meeting in 2h. :thumbsup:
